### CANDIDATE DETAIL
#### 1. Bernard-Soulier syndrome, type A2, autosomal dominant  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.447)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-9673221, Reactome:R-HSA-9769739, Reactome:R-HSA-9769743, Reactome:R-HSA-9935598)

**Proposed mechanism:** GP1BA (HGNC:4400) —DECREASES→ Thrombocytopenia (HP:0001873); Thrombocytopenia (HP:0001873) —LEADS_TO→ Abnormal platelet aggregation (HP:0030118); Abnormal platelet aggregation (HP:0030118) —LEADS_TO→ Bleeding (HP:0011420); GP1BA (HGNC:4400) —DECREASES→ Thrombocytopenia (HP:0001873); Thrombocytopenia (HP:0001873) —LEADS_TO→ Abnormal platelet aggregation (HP:0030118); Abnormal platelet aggregation (HP:0030118) —LEADS_TO→ Bleeding (HP:0011420). Loss-of-function mutations in GP1BA lead to reduced expression or function of the GPIb-IX-V complex, impairing platelet adhesion to von Willebrand factor. This results in thrombocytopenia, abnormal platelet aggregation, and bleeding, manifesting as common phenotypes in both diseases.

**How to falsify it:** The presence of pathogenic variants in GP1BA in individuals with MONDO:0012897 that result in a gain-of-function or dominant-negative effect, rather than loss-of-function, would falsify this hypothesis. _(variant: Exome or genome sequencing data from gnomAD showing a high frequency (>1%) of common variants in GP1BA that are not associated with either disease phenotype.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared genetic basis and functional consequences of GP1BA mutations in these distinct disease contexts could inform therapeutic strategies targeting platelet function and hemostasis for both conditions.

#### 2. Bernard-Soulier syndrome  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.438)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-9673221, Reactome:R-HSA-9769739, Reactome:R-HSA-9769743, Reactome:R-HSA-9935598)

**Proposed mechanism:** GP1BA (HGNC:4411) —DISRUPTS→ Glycoprotein Ib-IX-V complex formation (GO:0007155); GP1BB (HGNC:4412) —DISRUPTS→ Glycoprotein Ib-IX-V complex formation (GO:0007155); GP9 (HGNC:4413) —DISRUPTS→ Glycoprotein Ib-IX-V complex formation (GO:0007155); Glycoprotein Ib-IX-V complex formation (GO:0007155) —LEADS_TO→ Platelet adhesion to von Willebrand factor (GO:0007590); Platelet adhesion to von Willebrand factor (GO:0007590) —LEADS_TO→ Platelet aggregation (GO:0002021); Platelet aggregation (GO:0002021) —LEADS_TO→ Thrombocytopenia (HP:0001873); Platelet aggregation (GO:0002021) —LEADS_TO→ Abnormal platelet aggregation (HP:0030115); Platelet aggregation (GO:0002021) —LEADS_TO→ Bleeding tendency (HP:0011421). Loss-of-function mutations in GP1BA, GP1BB, or GP9 disrupt the formation and function of the glycoprotein Ib-IX-V complex, which is critical for platelet adhesion to von Willebrand factor and subsequent platelet aggregation. This cascade failure leads to thrombocytopenia, abnormal platelet aggregation, and bleeding tendency, common to both MONDO:0012897 and Bernard-Soulier syndrome.

**How to falsify it:** The identification of pathogenic variants in GP1BA, GP1BB, or GP9 that lead to gain-of-function or dominant-negative effects, or the absence of any defects in platelet adhesion and aggregation pathways in individuals diagnosed with MONDO:0012897, would falsify this hypothesis. _(variant: Pathogenic variants in GP1BA, GP1BB, or GP9 with a frequency > 0.1% in gnomAD.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared mechanism involving the glycoprotein Ib-IX-V complex can inform the development of targeted therapies for bleeding disorders associated with platelet dysfunction, potentially leading to novel treatments for both MONDO:0012897 and Bernard-Soulier syndrome.

Loss-of-function mutations in F9 (hemophilia B) and F11 (Factor XI deficiency) both disrupt the coagulation cascade, leading to impaired thrombin generation and an increased risk of bleeding.

**How to falsify it:** Demonstration that mutations in F9 and F11 do not converge on a common functional pathway within the coagulation cascade, or that the bleeding phenotype in one of the diseases is not a direct consequence of impaired coagulation. _(variant: Absence of pathogenic loss-of-function variants in F11 or F9 in populations with normal coagulation function.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared pathway of the coagulation cascade allows for potential therapeutic strategies that could target common downstream effectors to treat bleeding disorders caused by defects in different clotting factors, such as Factor XI replacement therapy for hemophilia C and Factor IX replacement therapy for hemophilia B.
